sections.heading: How to Play Survival
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Survival"][color=c3]Survival Hunter Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

The rotation for Survival Hunter focuses on a streamlined resource management loop. In simplest terms, you'll use as many as possible [spell=259489] in any given fight to generate enough [spell=260285] to buff most, if not all, of your other abilities. The important thing to keep in mind is that you don't want to use [spell=259489] too aggressively, as that means you'll waste the Focus it generates and waste Tip of the Spear stacks. 



[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name= ability_hunter_killcommand size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c3]Resource Management:[/color][/b] By far, the most important core to learn as a Survival Hunter is your resource management. Your [spell=259489] ability is limited by charges and cooldown, and Kill Command is responsible for generating both your resources: [color=druid]Focus[/color] and [spell=260285]. The best way to improve your play is to use Kill Command as much as possible in any given encounter, without over-capping on Focus or Tip of the Spear stacks. In practice, with the optimal talent build, this means you are using two abilities between each use of Kill Command. 
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name= ability_hunter_raptorstrike size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c3]Resource Spending:[/color][/b] Tying into the above point, it's very important you're spending your resources in a controlled way, while also maximizing the uses of your [spell=186270] without idling too much.  Due to our Apex node, more Raptor Strike means more [spell=1259003], which means you're missing tons of free damage if you're either spending too much (or too little!) Focus.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name= inv_wildfirebomb size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c3]Cooldown Management:[/color][/b] Two of your strongest abilities, [spell=259495] and [spell=1261193] are limited by cooldowns. It's important you're keeping these cooldowns in mind, as if you miss a use this can have a cascading effect further down the line and greatly lower your damage over any given encounter, especially in AoE.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=32403 icon=ability_hunter_camouflage]Survival Hunter Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

Your goal is to make sure as many of your abilities are being buffed by these as possible, while also using [spell=259495] and [spell=1261193] as frequently as possible.

sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
Before any combat happens, it is important for Survival Hunters to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.
[center][wrapper width=800px][box]
[ul]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Summon your pet -[/b] [color=q0]Make sure to summon a pet with a [span class=tip tooltip=PetSpecialization][color=hunter]Pet Specialization[/color][/span] suited for the content.[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Apply Hunter's Mark -[/b] [color=q0]Use [spell=257284] on the boss or strongest mob in a pack, increasing all damage on that target by 3%. If playing with multiple [color=hunter]hunters[/color], each should pick a different target. [/color][/li]
[/ul]
[/box][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c3][icon name=ability_hunter_camouflage type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Survival Hunter Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Survival has access to only a handful of cooldowns in the talent trees; some of them can only be picked up very deep into the tree, meaning you won't often pair them together.

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Takedown" icon=Inv12_ability_hunter_takedown]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=Inv12_ability_hunter_takedown type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon][color=hunter] Takedown [/color][/h3]
[spell=1250646] Is an extremely short-duration damage cooldown which should always be buffed with [spell=260285]. In addition to its high upfront damage, it buffs you and your pets' damage by 20%. It is worth noting that this 20% buff does not affect any damage sources outside of our class-specific damaging abilities, so no trinkets or non-class procs can be buffed this way.
Some talents affect [spell=1250646] in various ways:
[pad]
[ul]
[li]
[spell=1256938] turns [spell=1250646]  into an impressively powerful AoE attack. This doesn't inherently change the way your cooldown works, but it may affect the way you'd want to time your cooldown. For instance, without [spell=1256938], you may want to use [spell=1256938] before the adds even spawn in, so you don't have to spend the global cooldown during the add's lifespan.
[/li]

[li]
[spell=1272139] allows [spell=1250646] to generate 3 stacks of [spell=260285], meaning less of your extremely short cooldown window is spent pressing [spell=259277], allowing you to press the buttons that deal more meaningful damage more often.
This talent somewhat conflicts with [symbol=wow-hero-talent-pack-leader] [b][color=orange-gem]Pack Leader[/color][/b]'s [spell=472741] talent, which already incentivizes you to follow up your [spell=1250646] with a [spell=259277] to trigger the stampede and beast as soon as possible.
[/li]
[/ul]

[pad]
However, the talents that fundamentally modify [spell=1256938] the most are all part of hero-talent specific interactions.

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-pack-leader] [b][color=orange-gem]Pack Leader[/color][/b], [spell=1250646], as mentioned before, is simply modified by [spell=472741]. This causes your next [spell=259277] to trigger [spell=201430] and any of the next [icon name=ability_hunter_pet_bear][/icon] [icon name=inv_misc_elitewyvern][/icon] [icon name=ability_hunter_pet_boar][/icon] [spell=471876] Beasts in the sequence.
This doesn't affect gameplay a whole lot beyond that, but it is worth noting that [spell=201430] aims in a direction based on your position relative to your target, which is useful to know when you're trying to optimise the fairly narrow AoE zone.

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-sentinel] [b][color=revered]Sentinel[/color][/b], talents impact [spell=1250646] to a much bigger degree, and are modified by [spell=1264902], [spell=1253852], and [spell=1253830].

[ul]
[li]
[spell=1264902] directly replaces [spell=1250646], using the same keybind, and is a powerful follow-up attack. [spell=1266081] by itself can be further modified by a choice node, either [spell=1264904] or [spell=1266069].
[/li]

[li]
[spell=1266069] is the only [spell=1266081] node that directly impacts the way you use [spell=1266081], delaying its use until you can benefit from the 10 seconds of [spell=259495] Cooldown Reduction.
[/li]

[li]
[spell=1253852] noticeably boosts the proc chance of [spell=1253601] during [spell=1250646], allowing you to chuck more dramatically stronger bombs. [spell=1266069] can be especially helpful for this in the event you continue to proc a bunch, reducing the odds for you to run out of bombs to spend your [spell=1266069] procs with.
[/li]
[/ul]

[pad]
[/tab]


[tab name="Boomstick" icon=inv_musket_04]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_musket_04 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon][color=hunter] Boomstick [/color][/h3]
[spell=1261193] Is a very high-damaging frontal cone channel that should always be used with [spell=260285]. It has a fairly long range that can be utilised to hit enemies that are ordinarily too spread out to properly hit while in melee range. A quick [spell=781] gets you to an ideal distance for something like this, but it isn't strictly necessary in most cases.


[ul]
[li]
[spell=1261193] is functionally a 45-second cooldown for single target purposes, or it can have cooldowns as low as 15 seconds while AoEing thanks to [spell=1262409], a staple talent pick for AoE builds.
[/li]
[li]
[spell=1261229] can be paired with this to create a feedback loop, causing a drastically more fast paced AoE rotation.

[/li]
[/ul]

Something to consider is that although boomstick deals an incredible amount of damage for a single button, it spends at least 2 globals effectively to channel. This makes its single target potency a lot weaker than it looks at a glance, Although it is still worth using, simply never using it at all only results in a ~2.5% dps loss, even when heavily invested into boomstick talents.

Due to the layout of the talent tree we cannot easily ignore these talents, but it may give you some context to how "unimportant" boomstick actually is for Single Target output, meaning if there is ever an opporunity to hold its use to utilise it for AoE, you should consider it.

[/tab]







[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c3][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Survival Hunter Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
In addition to [spell=1251717] optimization, Survival Hunter has two other main points of optimization to truly separate yourself from a novice to more advanced Survival player. 
[pad]


[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Strike as One" icon=inv_coordinatedassault]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3] Strike as One [/color][/h3]
	[spell=1251717], despite being a passive talent, is one of your most important sources of damage. It's very important you're proccing this as much as possible, which means you're playing around your Focus management and [spell=259489] charges.
[/tab]
[tab name="Positioning" icon=inv_musket_04]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3] Positioning [/color][/h3]
	As a Survival Hunter, literally all of your AoE/Cleave depends on your positioning. [spell=259495] and [spell=1261193] deal their damage in a cone (from the target and from you respectively) so you need to be aware of your position and place yourself in an angle to hit as many targets as possible with the abilities conal shape.  [spell=1259003] and [spell=472741] also rely on your positioning as well, so it's a good idea to keep track of where you are in relation to the target(s).
[/tab]
[tab name="Pet Utility" icon=spell_hunter_lonewolf]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3]Pet Utility [/color][/h3]
	To make sure you're meeting you and your groups needs at all times, we strongly recommend you keep a Tenacity, Ferocity, and Cunning pet in your active pet slots at all times. This means you can flex into more self-sustain and Bloodlust with Ferocity, more pure damage reduction through Tenacity, or external CC cleansing with Cunning.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Survival Hunter guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Survival Hunter guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].



[tooltip name=OBR_with][color=q]Utilizing your cooldowns as they become available, timing them with other cooldowns, and overlapping properly.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=OBR_without][color=q]Following the Assisted Combat suggestions exactly, or only pressing the Single-Button without any other buttons being used.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=TotSexplain]
[color=prismatic-gem]Tip of the Spear benefits[/color]
Beyond just the damage benefit, spending Tip of the Spear is also the "engine" to trigger [spell=1251717], which deals massive damage just by itself, especially as [color=orange-gem]pack leader[/color]. 

When playing [color=exalted]Sentinel[/color], [spell=1253601] applications also trigger through Tip of the Spear consumptions. Additionally, Tip of the Spear is further enhanced through [spell=1253830] and [spell=1253751].[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=HeroTalentchoice]
[color=prismatic-gem]Hero talent impact on talent choice[/color]
[color=orange-gem]Pack leader[/color] Focuses on [spell=186270] and pet damage, massively buffing [spell=1251717] through hero talent nodes such as [spell=472357] and [spell=471878].
Because [spell=472660] is already part of the hero talent tree, [spell=1253172] becomes a more valid pick, and as a result [spell=260248] is slightly more lucrative as well.

[color=exalted]Sentinel[/color] emphasises [spell=259495], through [spell=1253601], and will instead opt for talents such as [spell=1253176] and [spell=378937][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=Takedownfocus]
There is no need to worry about the focus Takedown generates. Actively dumping focus often means you will have to spend multiple untipped [spell=186270]s, which is not worth it.
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=TakedownfocusTF]
There is no need to worry about the focus [spell=1250646] generates. Actively dumping focus often means you will have to spend multiple untipped [spell=186270]s, which is not worth it.

Using [spell=1250646] at 1 [stack of spell=260285] means it will still benefit, while also generating the maximum possible stacks from [spell=1272139].
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=Hogstrider]
This is a bit of an unusual priority step, but given that both the ability and effect are new, it is worth emphasising. 

Even when tripling [spell=193265] damage, it still falls short of baseline [spell=186270]s, not even counting any of the enhancing talents. Furthermore, [spell=193265] cannot benefit from [spell=472352], making the ability a waste of focus unless you find yourself outside of melee range without [spell=186289].
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=Howl]
"Any beasts available" effectively means having any of the [icon name=ability_hunter_pet_bear][/icon] [icon name=inv_misc_elitewyvern][/icon] [icon name=ability_hunter_pet_boar][/icon] "buffs" active, and thus summoning them by using [spell=34026].
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=HogstriderAoE]
This is barely worth using at 5 or more targets, and not worth using at any less. Consider holding it and using it as a means to exit melee range for a GCD if you feel like you might need to do something, such as avoid a ground slam.
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=PetSpecialization]
[color=prismatic-gem]Pet Specialization[/color]

You can change your pet's specialization at any stable master, and it is generally convenient to have at least 1 pet of every specialization with you at all times, each providing unique effects that affect both your pet and yourself.

[color=hunter][b]Tenacity[/b][/color]
Tenacity pets are great for providing passive damage mitigation and effective health, which is extremely valuable in content where you frequently get hit for large amounts of damage, such as high-end Mythic+.

[spell=388035] - Damage taken reduced by 3%.
[spell=264662] - Max HP increased by 5% 

[color=hunter][b]Ferocity[/b][/color]
Ferocity pets are great for constant passive healing, and can usually offset more damage than a [color=hunter]Tenacity[/color] could, but it often doesn't help you live an Effective Health damage intake "check" which can occur frequently in high m+.

[spell=264663] - Grants you and your pet 4% Leech.
[spell=264667] - Typically known as "bloodlust", a 30% haste buff for the entire raid group on a 10-minute shared cooldown.

[color=hunter][b]Cunning[/b][/color]
Cunning pets are essential for PvP, but can have some niche uses for PVE as well, most notably when certain damage abilities can be outright immuned through [spell=53271] due to having a slowing effect attached.

[spell=53271] - Grants your target and your pet 4 seconds of immunity to root and slowing effects, and charges your pet to your target. This charge component can be useful in niche situations where your pet cannot keep up with you when running large distances.
[spell=264656] - Gives you and your pet 8% movement speed.
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=stackmob]
This allows you to hold on to your stronger AoE abilities, such as [spell=259495] and [spell=1261215] until mobs are properly stacked, as well as attempt to generate a lucky [spell=1253601] or two. 
[/tooltip]
